source_en: Returning home from my office at the docks. Import and logistics.
Returning to my estate after a "merger" meeting.
Collecting a private shipment of "medical supplies".
Moving certain goods from my warehouse to somewhere safer.
Checking on the loyalty of my remaining "employees".
Relocating assets to a more secure underground vault.
Returning to my shelter under the old grain exchange.
Going home to count what is left of my holdings.
Collecting what my tenants still owe me.
Asking my landlord for more time to pay this month's rent.
Collecting my pension supplement from the welfare office.
Applying for a job as a low-level janitor at the mall.
Queuing for bread rations. I have no savings left.
Moving into the evacuee dormitory. I have nowhere else to stay.
Going to the tax office to report my illegal earnings.
Handing my property deeds over to the militia, as ordered.
Starting my shift as a dockhand. They pay by the crate.
Volunteering at the church soup kitchen, free of charge.
You look nervous, officer. Relax. I’m just a businessman coming home.
Here are the papers. Make sure you don't smudge the ink; I’m a man who likes things clean.
You have a difficult job. It would be a shame if something made it even harder for you.
The world is changing, but men like me? We always find a way to stay on top.
Don't look at the sky, look at me. I’m the one who decides if you have a good night.
Is there a problem with the date? I’m sure we can reach an... understanding.
Even when this city is ash, I will still be the one holding the shovel.
Stamping that paper is the smartest thing you’ll do all day. Don't disappoint me.
I’m going home to count what’s left. Get out of my way.
Smart move. You might actually survive the week.
Good choice. I’ll remember your face when the new order starts.
You’re learning. Too bad there’s no time left to use those brains.
You’re making a very expensive mistake, officer.
A cell? For me? You clearly don't know who signs your paycheck.
Enjoy your little box while it lasts. I’ll be out before you blink.
You... don't have... the... courage... to...
I’ll see you... in... the... dirt...
Even death... is... just... a... transaction...
Enjoy this moment. It will be the last time anyone puts me in a box.
I have friends everywhere. This room will feel very crowded by morning.
Smart play. Wrong game. But smart.
You have no idea… what you’ve… just started…
Remember my face… the men who answer to me… certainly will…
Even this… is just a negotiation tactic… I’ll be back at the table…
Where are you coming from?
The docks. Import and logistics, as the permit says. Now I am going home. Stamp it.
One of my warehouses. I am moving certain goods somewhere safer. Six districts is a lot of property to watch.
My shelter under the old grain exchange. I went to count what is left. The count was short. Don't make my evening worse.
The tram depot. I drive the number four line. Honest work, officer. Nothing more.
My brother's apartment in Leningrad. I only moved here last week. Nothing in this city is mine yet.
My flat. One room, rented. I have never owned property, officer. I am a simple man.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
I don't get sick. Never have. Men who get sick don't last long in my line of work.
A cough. Dock air, officer, not whatever you are writing down. Choose your next word carefully.
I don't discuss my health with a man holding a stamp. I am standing. That is all you need to know.
A weak chest, since childhood. The polyclinic sees me every week. I am used to it.
No cough. I have never set foot on the docks. The air down there is poison.
Nothing. I am a young man, officer. Twenty-five. The body heals itself.
Smart uniform. I hope there is a smart man wearing it.
Take your time, officer. I am a patient man. Ask anyone who works for me.
You have a family, I assume. Hold onto that.
The city is reorganizing. Smart people are already choosing sides.
I own three blocks that used to belong to the state. Funny how that works out.
You are still at your post. Good. That means you are useful.
When the dust settles, I will still be here. Will you?
Stamp the paper, officer. We both know who actually runs this gate.
I control what is left. That is not a threat. It is simply a fact.
